Your Own Git Repo¶

You will want to begin with setting up your own Git repo. If you are unfamiliar with Git, then you should read up on it, and/or do some tutorials. It is beyond the scope of this documentation to teach Git.

There are some 3rd party Git GUI tools that you could use to help, especially if you don’t like the command line interface of Git. Consider these,

https://www.gitkraken.com/git-client (not free, works everywhere)

https://www.sourcetreeapp.com (free, Windows/Max only)

https://git-scm.com/download/gui/linux (list of others)

Command Line (Mirroring)¶

Use this method to create a private copy of a public repository that includes all branches and tags. (There are other approaches if you are familiar with git.)

1. Create a bare clone of the public repository¶

This pulls down the underlying git data without creating a working directory.

git clone --bare https://github.com/sistemicorp/scripts

2. Create a new private repository on GitHub¶

Go to GitHub and create a new repository.

Important

  • Do not initialize it with a README, .gitignore, or License.

  • Set the visibility to Private.

3. Mirror-push to your new private repository¶

Move into the bare clone directory and push everything to your new private URL.

cd scripts.git
git push --mirror https://github.com/yourname/private-repo.git

4. Clean up and clone locally¶

Remove the temporary bare clone folder and perform a standard clone of your new private repo to begin working.

cd ..
rm -rf scripts.git
git clone https://github.com/yourname/private-repo.git

Install Git Hooks¶

Git Hooks are generally replaced by Git Actions and are beyond the scope of these instructions

In the scripts repo, there is a folder called hooks. The contents of this folder needs to be copied to ./.git/hooks folder of your repository.

Depending on your directory structure, this example command may work,

cd ~/git/scripts
cp hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/

This githook will update public/VERSION file that Prism uses to display the version of the scripts. A change to public/VERSION is also what makes Lente rebuild the scripts package for stations. By using this githook, or some other mechanism, the script version is tracked by Prism. The version number is derived from a tag.

Create a Tag¶

The Sistemi system reports the version of things to help keep you organized, including the version of your scripts.

On whatever branch you decide to “release” your scripts, for example, the “main” branch, create a tag on that branch. The tag MUST be of this format,

V.v

where:
    V - is major revision, manually increased by YOU, be making a new Tag
    v - is minor revision, manually increased by YOU, be making a new Tag

Example commands to create (and push) a tag,

git checkout master
git tag 1.0
git push origin --tags

The version uses the most recent tag (git describe –tags). For example, version 0.9.12 is the 12th commit after tag 0.9. scripts already has tags (for example 0.8), you can remove them from your fork,

git tag --delete 0.8
git push origin --delete 0.8

Change README.md¶

Change this file to suit your needs. For example, document your script/program naming strategy.

Installing Python¶

Prism uses Python version 3.12 inside its Docker container, and therefore that specific version should be used for development. Ubuntu 24.04 includes Python 3.12.

Install dependencies from requirements.txt into a virtual environment,

sudo apt install python3.12-dev python3.12-venv
cd ~/git/scripts
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Command Line Development¶

Initial development will be done in “headless” mode, whereupon coding is done outside of the GUI used in production.

A command line version of the core engine of the system is at the top of the scripts folder, called prism_dev.py. The command line help,

(.venv) martin@computer:~/git/scripts$ python prism_dev.py --help
usage: prism_dev.py [-h] --script SCRIPT [--lint] [--result-scan]

prism_dev

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --script SCRIPT  Path to script file to run
  --lint           Only lint the script and its test code, exit 1 on errors
  --result-scan    Scan result file for correctness

Usage examples:
    python prism_dev.py --script ./public/prism/scripts/example/prod_v0/prod_0.scr
    python prism_dev.py --script ./public/prism/scripts/example/pybrd_v0/pybrd_0.scr
    python prism_dev.py --lint --script ./public/prism/scripts/example/prod_v0/prod_1.scr

Sistemi Corporation, copyright, all rights reserved, 2019-2025

Notes about the command line development environment,

  • parallel, multi-threaded, multiple test jigs are not supported

    • script is run as a single thread - cannot test parallelism

    • however your code will run multiple jigs in parallel within the Prism GUI

  • Results are NOT sent to the Lente Server, however a local Result file with the results will be created for inspection purposes.

  • script substitutions are filled in without asking, each sub uses its default, or else its first choices entry, or else a placeholder (prismdev, or 0 for a num sub). The values used are logged. To try other values, change the defaults while developing, or use the helper script prism_subs.py, which needs to be modified per script it is used on.

  • the script is linted before it runs, see Script Lint

After your script is running in the command line mode, you can try it in the Prism GUI.

Script Lint¶

The script linter, public/prism/script_lint.py, checks a script and the Python test items it runs, without running them. It finds mistakes that would otherwise only show up on the production floor, such as a test item that returns without calling self.item_end().

The test modules are read as source code and are not imported, so no driver or hardware code runs. Only the methods named by the script’s items are checked.

The linter runs,

  • with python prism_dev.py --lint --script <script>, which only lints and exits with 1 if there are errors. The script may have a subs section, and its subs are checked too. This is a good step to add to your CI.

  • before every prism_dev.py run. An error stops the run.

  • when you Validate a script in Prism, after substitutions. An error rejects the script, and warnings are shown in the notices.

Findings are ERROR or WARN, and each one names where it is. A script problem names the script section, and a code problem names the file, line and item,

ERROR info.lot: longer than 16 characters
ERROR tests[0].items[3] TST003: no method TST003 in public.prism.scripts.my_v0.tst00xx
ERROR public/prism/scripts/my_v0/tst00xx.py:212 TST001_Meas: return before item_end()
WARN public/prism/scripts/my_v0/tst00xx.py:240 TST006_RsrcLock: time.sleep() cannot be stopped by a timeout, use self.sleep()

Test item checks¶

Every path through a test item method is followed, including early returns in if, try, with, match and loops.

Errors,

  • the first statement, after the doc string, must be ctx = self.item_start()

  • self.item_start() must be called only once

  • every path must end with self.item_end(), and every return must come right after it (or be return self.item_end(...)). Raising an exception is allowed; Prism ends the item as INTERNAL_ERROR.

  • self.item_end() must not be called twice on one path. This usually means a missing return after an early self.item_end().

  • a result passed as a string must be a ResultAPI.RECORD_RESULT_* value

  • self.item_end(_next="<id>") must name an item that comes later in the script

  • ctx.item.args.<name>, ctx.item.args["<name>"], ctx.item.<field>, ctx.options.<name> and ctx.config.<name> must exist in the script. Use ctx.item.args.get("<name>", <default>) for an optional value.

  • the module file must exist, with a class of the same name as the file, and a method for every item id

Warnings, for code that a timeout cannot stop (see Timeouts and Aborts),

  • time.sleep(), use self.sleep()

  • a while loop that never calls self.sleep(), self.check_abort() or an input method

  • a bare except: or except BaseException: that does not re-raise, use except Exception:

The linter is strict: it does not follow calls into your own helper methods. A helper that calls self.item_end() does not count as ending the item, so call self.item_end() in the test item method itself.

Script checks¶

Errors,

  • info must have product, bom, lot and location (config is optional), as strings no longer than the Lente database fields (see info). Empty strings are allowed. Other fields are errors, as Lente cannot store them.

  • config.drivers must be a non-empty list of driver module names, or [module, args] pairs, and each driver module must exist

  • fail_fast must be true or false

  • tests, each module and each items list must be present and non-empty

  • an item enable must be true or false, or the strings "true" / "false" from a str sub

  • a timeout must be a positive number

  • args and options must be objects

  • fail must be a list of {"fid": ..., "msg": ...}

  • after substitution, no "%%<key>" may be left in the script

Checks of the subs section, when linting a script before substitution (see subs),

  • each "%%<key>" in the script must be defined in subs, or as an inner sub (error)

  • each sub must have a type of str or num, and a widget of textinput or select; a select must have choices (error)

  • a regex must compile, and the default must match it (error)

  • inner subs must have an entry for every choice, given as {"val": ..., "type": ...}, and must not reuse a top level key (error)

  • a sub that is never used is a warning

Warnings,

  • an item field that looks like a typo of enable, timeout, args or fail, for example "timout". Items may carry other fields for your code, read as ctx.item.<field>.

  • the last item of a test is disabled. The last item is the teardown and should always run.
